[{#aTa-f-vanip SakanDvAdi˚#} <ls>Tv.</ls>; probably connected
 with some word like {%athar%} fire]
_meanings:
.²1 A priest who has to worship fire and Soma.
.²2 A Brāhmaṇa.
.²3 <ab>N.</ab> of the priest who is said to have first brought down fire from the
 heaven, offered Soma and recited prayers. [He is represented as the eldest
 son of Brahmā sprung from his mouth; as a Prajāpati appointed by Brahmā
 to create and protect subordinate beings, who first learnt from Brahmā
 and then taught the Brahmavidyā and is considered to be the author of
 the Veda called after him. His wife was Śānti, daughter of Kardama Prajāpati.
 He had also another wife called Chitti; he is also considered identical
 with Aṅgiras and father of Agni.]
.²4 Epithet of Śiva, Vasiṣṭha. {#vftapadapaNktiraTarvaReva vedaH#} <ls>Ki. 10. 10</ls>.
--(<ab>pl.</ab>) Descendants of Atharvan; hymns of this Veda; {#jizRuM jEtrEraTarvaBiH#} <ls>R. 17. 13</ls>.

The Atharvaveda, regarded as the
 fourth Veda. [It contains many forms of imprecations for the destruction
 of enemies and also contains a great number of prayers for safety and
 averting mishaps, evils, sins or calamities, and a number of hymns, as
 in the other Vedas, addressed to the gods with prayers to be used at religious
 and solemn rites; <ab>cf.</ab> <ls>Mv. 2. 24</ls>. {#mUrtimaBirAmaGorAM biBradivATarvaRo#}
 {#nigamaH#}. It has nine Śākhās and five Kalpas, and is comprised in 20
 Kāṇḍas. The most important Brāhmaṇa belonging to this Veda is the
 Gopatha-Brāhmaṇa, and the Upaniṣads pertaining to it are stated to
 be 52, or, according to another account 31.] [<ab>cf.</ab> <lang>Zend.</lang> {%atharvan%}, <lang>Pers.</lang>
 {%āturbān%}.]
(<ab>pl.</ab>) those who have become Atharvans, Names of the 12 Maharṣis.

<ab>N.</ab> of an Upaniṣad dealing with Brahmavidyā. {#aTarvaSiraso'DyetA#}
 {#brahmacArI yatavrataH#} <ls>Mb. 13. 90. 29</ls>.

A text of collection of hymns of {#aTarvaveda#}. {#aTarvasaMhitAyAjI#}
